{"self_assessment": "Impact
I kept the table supplied so the builders never had to stop. I made two full 40-domino runs to the boxes, 80 dominoes into the shared bin. Big batches cost about 60 seconds per trip, which is much cheaper per domino than small ones. I also built the lower tail of the fish (stroke 4), 14 dominoes traced from the bottom line out to its tip. That finished the tail, which is one of the features that makes the outline read as a fish. Before the push, the run was tracing as roughly 88 of 93 standing dominoes connected to the start.

Execution
I took the lower tail when Priya asked and kept to it, laying it in short steady bursts. I reported progress honestly (ten of fourteen, then done) so the others could plan around it. The tail reached its end and looked dark, meaning connected, all the way from the bump. After that I kept spare dominoes ready in case a patch was needed.

Collaboration
I answered every request directly, confirmed my assignment and kept the others updated on my progress. I stayed out of the nose area once it was marked hands-off. Two people working close together risk bumping each other's lines, so keeping clear protected the work already standing. I did not add anything that could disturb the connected run in the final minutes.

Leadership
My leadership was mostly in supporting the plan. I committed to the lower tail, finished it ahead of the 5-minute mark, and kept the supply from becoming a bottleneck. I stayed disciplined once the picture was complete: hands off, no unnecessary changes. I believe the fish was built efficiently as a team, with my part being the supply and the lower tail.", "my_share_percent": 25}
